description.value: A mote is a tiny split-second of time that a time mage steals from his own future. Each day, the time mage has a pool of motes equal to his time mage level. Once per round as a free action, even outside of their turn, a time mage can expend a mote to take a swift action that does not count against his normal limit of one swift action per round for time mage class features or spells, or gain a bonus to one skill check, ability check, saving throw, or caster level check on a single action within one round, equal to +1d3 (increasing to +2d3 at 8th level and +3d3 at 16th level). At 3rd level, by spending a mote, the time mage can extend any spell he casts that has a variable duration by a number of rounds equal to the bonus above. At 7th level, he may spend a mote to reduce the duration of any negative condition or effect he is suffering by 1d6 rounds (2d6 at 15th level, minimum 0). At 11th level, he may spend a mote to take a move action as a swift action. At 15th level, he can spend a mote to cast a spell with a casting time of 1 standard action or less as a swift action, and cannot cast any other spell that round. At 19th level, he may use a mote to grant any ally within 60 feet an additional move action on that ally's next turn. A time mage may gain additional options for use of a mote by taking temporal talents, though he is still restricted to spending motes only once each round.
